terms.definition: Raw facts collected from the real world that have no inherent meaning by themselves
terms.example: 'Vikram', '500', 'Mysuru' are data points — meaningless without context

terms.definition: Data that has been processed, structured, or combined to give it meaning
terms.example: A table showing 'Vikram attended AWS workshop in Mysuru for ₹500' is information

terms.definition: Data that describes other data — information about a file or record rather than its content
terms.example: A photo's metadata includes file size, date taken, GPS location, and file format

terms.definition: Data organized in a fixed format with rows and columns, each following a defined schema
terms.example: An Excel spreadsheet of student grades with fixed columns: ID, Name, Grade, City

terms.definition: Data with no fixed format that cannot be organized into rows and columns
terms.example: Images, videos, audio files, PDF documents, and social media posts

terms.definition: Data that uses tags or key-value pairs for organization but does not follow a fixed table schema
terms.example: A JSON file with user profile data where different users can have different fields

terms.definition: An organized collection of data stored electronically for easy access, management, and retrieval
terms.example: A MySQL database storing student enrollment records for a university

terms.definition: Database Management System — software that creates, manages, and provides access to databases
terms.example: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and Microsoft SQL Server are all DBMS software

terms.definition: Structured Query Language — the standard language for interacting with relational databases
terms.example: SELECT * FROM students WHERE city = 'Mysuru' retrieves students from Mysuru

terms.definition: Data Definition Language — SQL commands that define database structure (CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE)
terms.example: CREATE TABLE students (id INT, name VARCHAR(100)) creates a new table structure

terms.definition: Data Manipulation Language — SQL commands that work with data inside tables (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE)
terms.example: INSERT INTO students VALUES (1, 'Vikram') adds a new row to the students table

terms.definition: A database data structure that speeds up SELECT queries by allowing direct lookup without full table scan
terms.example: An index on the city column makes WHERE city = 'Mysuru' queries much faster

terms.definition: Amazon Relational Database Service — a fully managed service that runs relational databases with automated backups, patching, and HA
terms.example: An RDS MySQL instance running your e-commerce application's product catalog database

terms.definition: The URL address AWS assigns to an RDS instance, used by applications and client tools to connect to the database
terms.example: mydb.cxyz123.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com — entered as hostname in MySQL Workbench

terms.definition: A read-only asynchronous copy of an RDS primary instance used to offload read queries and improve performance
terms.example: Directing all SELECT queries to a read replica while writes go to the primary instance

terms.definition: RDS feature that maintains a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone for automatic failover (high availability)
terms.example: Primary RDS in us-east-1a, standby in us-east-1b — automatic failover in ~60 seconds if primary fails

terms.definition: AWS-native cloud relational database engine with MySQL and PostgreSQL compatibility, 6x copies across 3 AZs, and up to 15 read replicas
terms.example: Aurora MySQL running a high-traffic social media app with 10 read replicas and 128 TB auto-scaling storage

terms.definition: Aurora mode that automatically starts, scales, and shuts down based on application demand — billed per second of actual use
terms.example: A development database that shuts down when not in use and scales up during testing sprints

terms.definition: Fully managed data warehouse service optimized for OLAP analytical queries across petabytes of historical data
terms.example: A BI team running annual sales trend analysis across 5 years of data from multiple source systems

terms.definition: Online Transaction Processing — database workload pattern for fast, short, many concurrent transactions (day-to-day operations)
terms.example: An e-commerce checkout system processing thousands of orders per minute — use RDS or Aurora

terms.definition: Online Analytical Processing — database workload pattern for complex queries across large historical datasets for analysis
terms.example: A finance team running quarterly revenue breakdowns across years of data — use Redshift

terms.definition: Fully managed in-memory caching service that stores frequently accessed data in RAM for sub-millisecond access
terms.example: Caching the top 100 products query result so it's served from memory instead of hitting RDS

terms.definition: In-memory data store supported by ElastiCache — feature-rich with persistence, replication, pub/sub, and complex data structures
terms.example: Storing user sessions, gaming leaderboards, and real-time pub/sub notifications

terms.definition: Simple, multi-threaded in-memory key-value cache supported by ElastiCache — no persistence, no replication
terms.example: Simple high-throughput caching of static data that is acceptable to lose on restart

terms.definition: Fully managed serverless NoSQL key-value and document database with single-digit millisecond performance at any scale
terms.example: A gaming app storing player data and leaderboards for millions of concurrent users worldwide
